title: Streaming Speech To Speech Moshi Hibiki
motto: 2024-2026 redefined voice AI. Moshi ships a single model that listens and speaks simultaneously at 200 ms latency. Hibiki does speech-to-speech translation chunk-by-chunk. Both abandon the ASR → LLM → TTS pipeline for a unified full-duplex architecture over Mimi codec tokens. This is the new reference design.

steps.title: Core idea
steps.body: 2024-2026 redefined voice AI. Moshi ships a single model that listens and speaks simultaneously at 200 ms latency. Hibiki does speech-to-speech translation chunk-by-chunk. Both abandon the ASR → LLM → TTS pipeline for a unified full-duplex architecture over Mimi codec tokens. This is the new reference design.

steps.title: Why this matters
cards: Every voice agent built from Lessons 11 + 12 has a fundamental latency floor around 300-500 ms: VAD fires, STT processes, LLM reasons, TTS generates. Each stage has its own minimum latency. You can tune and parallelize, but the pipeline shape caps you.

Moshi (Kyutai, 2024-2026) asks a different question: what if there is no pipeline? What if one model takes audio in and emits audio out directly, continuously, with text as an intermediate "inner monologue" instead of a required stage?

steps.title: The concept
steps.body: Full-duplex speech-to-speech models stream audio in and out.

steps.title: Implement s2s
steps.body: Write the function from scratch in the workspace. Run when ready — all tests must pass.

def duplex_latency_ms(capture, infer, play):
    return capture+infer+play
